content.comment_body: Hello, I recently moved into an apartment and discovered that the electrical system is managed by a [product_name] (older model with a display). Unfortunately, I accidentally erased the program and there was no backup, so we're unable to operate the lights. I'm not experienced with programming, but I've investigated how things are connected: for instance, Q6 is the bathroom light and I1 is its switch. When I attempt to create a program such as I1 -> Q6, the light only flashes when the switch is pressed and stays on if held, turning off again when released. Our switches are not standard—they're multi-push types. I'm programming directly on the device's display since I lack the necessary cables and software. My goal is simply to have: press I1 to turn on, press I2 to turn off, like typical on/off behavior. Apologies for my English, I'm from Denmark. [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Check out a video tutorial to get a sense of the programming steps. Look for the RS function if you wish to use two inputs; the options available depend on your [product_name]'s [version_no]. If you have [version_no] 0BA0, only RS is available; at 0BA1 or newer, you can achieve this even with one input. If you can access a computer, try downloading the trial version of [product_name] programming software—it's free. The software and upgrades can be found on the [company_name] site ([url]). Observe the last digits of your product code—for example: [article_no]—as the digit indicates your specific version. Higher numbers mean more functions. When starting the software, open a new project and press CTRL+H to choose your version.
Hi, Why use two inputs if you can achieve this with one? Every model of this device has a Pulse Relay, so a single press toggles the output: first press turns it on, next turns it off. Regards,

Thank you for your help. Now it's working. Is it possible to control Q1 from multiple switches—like having I1 and I2 both operate Q1? For example, we'd like to switch the bathroom light (Q1) from the bedroom (I1), but also maintain the normal bathroom switch (I2). [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user lost control of their apartment lighting after unintentionally deleting the program on a [product_name] (with display) and had no backup. They faced difficulty restoring basic on/off functions using just the built-in interface, encountering problems with momentary switch actions and retaining the light state. Community members provided suggestions on finding the necessary logic functions, highlighted version differences, and pointed to tutorials and software for easier setup. Main challenges included the system’s complexity for beginners, lack of guidance when programming directly on the hardware, and difficulty configuring multi-way switches without external software.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to restore and configure straightforward on/off and multi-way light switching using pushbutton controls in their apartment, without needing cables, additional software, or programming expertise.
